title: Malaysia’s insurance supervisor asks what customers are getting from policies they keep
summary: A policy still in force a year after purchase is a useful business outcome for an insurer. It is a less complete measure of whether a family can afford the cover or rely on it when a claim arises. At Malaysia’s Asian Quality Business Awards, Bank Negara Malaysia Assistant Governor Norhana Endut used the distinction to explain what she expects of insurers, takaful operators and the intermediaries who sell their products. She placed suitability and continuing service alongside retention. For investors comparing distribution franchises, her remarks offer a set of questions to ask about the quality of recurring premiums.

The speech’s most specific evidence is the 2024/25 customer satisfaction survey. Footnote 2 reports service efficiency as the leading driver at 38.2%, followed by suitability at 28.7%, accessibility at 20.7% and transparency of claims at 12.5%. These percentages refer to the reported drivers of satisfaction. They cannot be read as the percentage of consumers whose claims were paid, or as ratings of individual insurers. Their ordering makes the point that a firm can invest in rapid transactions and still leave material concerns about appropriate coverage or access unresolved.

Persistency features in recognition at the awards. Footnote 3 defines it by purchase cohort, measuring the share of policies that remain in force at successive durations under the reporting framework for distribution channels. That is a useful distinction for comparing businesses. A large flow of new sales can lift total policy count while older customers allow coverage to lapse. Conversely, a high renewal rate does not reveal whether customers understand exclusions, whether the cover remains adequate, or what it costs them to keep it. The speech supplies no individual insurer results and sets no new retention target.

Endut linked this point to two strands of supervisory work. The exposure draft on proper advice practices for insurance and takaful was published on 30 September. Its stated objective is advice grounded in the customer’s needs and circumstances, including whether a recommendation serves the customer beyond completion of a sale. In medical protection, the industry’s MediAsas work under the RESET initiative aims to support affordable, sustainable coverage as health-care costs rise. The revised medical and health insurance and takaful policy document was expected by year-end at the time of the remarks. The speech announces neither final advice requirements nor new pricing terms for a specific policy.

The operational question for distributors is what changes before and after the customer signs. Endut called for advisers to establish customer circumstances, build competence as products grow more complicated and maintain transparent contact over the policy’s life. Better technology can improve access and give advisers information to make recommendations. Whether those recommendations actually fit the customer remains a matter of professional judgment. From the perspective of a business model, that points to assessing renewal cohorts, advice quality, servicing and claims handling together. An increase in digital sales or faster processing, viewed alone, would miss much of the performance the supervisor describes.

questions.question: Which distribution channels retain customers with coverage that continues to meet their needs?
questions.detail: Compare like-for-like policy cohorts at similar durations and premium levels, using the reporting definition in footnote 3. Examine why customers lapse, reduce cover or complain, alongside renewals. Persistency becomes a more informative indicator of franchise quality when a reader can distinguish a sustained relationship with useful protection from one in which coverage or affordability has deteriorated.

questions.question: What would establish that stronger advice standards change the recommendations customers receive?
questions.detail: Look for how intermediaries document needs, explain exclusions and revisit affordability when circumstances change. Compare the exposure draft with the final instrument when available, then examine the same channels before and after implementation. Evidence on complaints, replacement sales and outcomes after a claim would provide a closer test of appropriateness than completion of training alone.

questions.question: Can more affordable medical protection remain usable as healthcare costs rise?
questions.detail: Follow the final medical and health insurance and takaful framework and the terms of MediAsas products. Changes in premiums, benefits, access and claims experience can affect affordability in different directions. Tracking households over renewal cycles would help determine whether the industry is extending durable protection or principally changing the initial price of entry.
